children: Emma Tucker
1. FROM MY DESK

President Trump once threatened to tariff Canada into becoming America's 51st state. Now, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is attempting an ambitious pivot toward Europe, with his team using diplomatic backchannels to negotiate an "associate member" status with the European Union. Canada is eyeing ways to informally lock into Europe's $21 trillion market so goods, services and workers in strategic industries like energy, AI and defense can move frictionlessly across the Atlantic. Our reporters explore how a network-including members of an exclusive Ottawa book club-is trying to pull off one of the most consequential geopolitical shifts in modern history.

And for sports fans tuning in for today's NFL slate, prepare for some wallet fatigue. The NFL's Sunday Ticket package is getting smaller-but certainly not cheaper. Driven by a bidding war among media companies, the league has moved more marquee games to stand-alone streaming windows, leaving Sunday Ticket subscribers with fewer games for the regular price tag of $378. Joe Flint breaks down how live sports' biggest power player is forcing fans and distributors to pay more for a shrinking lineup.

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you're not subscribed, sign up here. If you're reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.
2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
Missouri's redistricting chaos has voters on both sides feeling disenfranchised as Democrats fend off continuing Republican efforts to use GOP-friendly voting maps.
Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan defeated Aryna Sabalenka in the U.S. Open women's final to claim her second major of the season and her third overall.
Jimmy Buffett's business manager and family members are locked in a messy legal battle over the late singer's $275 million trust.
Republicans are pouring tens of millions into Texas to rescue Ken Paxton's struggling Senate bid as polls show him trailing Democrat James Talarico.
3. FROM THE MARKETS

After years of losing ground, Tesla once again accounts for more than half of all U.S. EV sales. The turnaround isn't driven by surging Tesla demand, but by legacy carmakers cutting production, delaying imports and scrapping affordable models.
4. READ IT HERE FIRST
The latest spot for a Trump Tower is an ex-Soviet republic moving closer to Russia.

U.S. relations with Georgia have gone from warm to frigid as the former Soviet republic has cracked down on dissent and swung closer to Russia. One American business is undeterred: the Trump Organization. Georgian developers are preparing to market a 70-story Trump Tower in Tbilisi that would be the country's tallest building. Adding to the foreign-policy discord, the tower could financially benefit the family of a Georgian billionaire sanctioned by the U.S. Eliot Brown and Evan Gershkovich detail the deal and the booming market for Trump towers abroad.
Anthropic wants the AI race to slow down. So why isn't it hitting the brakes?

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on the AI industry to slow the development of cutting-edge technology, and rivals Sam Altman and Elon Musk said they agree. But Amodei stopped short of doing the one thing in his power: slowing Anthropic's own work. That gets at a moral conflict playing out inside the company, which was founded in part over concerns that OpenAI wasn't taking safety seriously enough. Anthropic's employees warn their technology could be dangerous, yet the company remains locked in a race to build it first. Tim Higgins examines the contradiction at the heart of one of the world's leading AI companies.

6. SEE THE STORY
Find out what it's really like to retire to a low-tax state.

Trading high-tax states for places like Florida, Arizona or Nevada can unlock home equity and shrink state income-tax bills. But lower-cost areas aren't always what they seem, as surging property taxes, HOA dues and insurance costs can quickly eat into expected savings. Seven retirees opened up to us about their finances, their tax breaks and the surprise expenses that came with their new ZIP Codes. Check out how their moves paid off.
7. HAPPENING THIS WEEK
Monday: The 78th Emmy Awards airs, with "Law & Order" star Mariska Hargitay hosting the ceremony.
Tuesday: The Federal Reserve interest-rate policy meeting begins.
Wednesday: The Fed concludes its two-day policy meeting with a rate decision. The Commerce Department releases August retail-sales data.
Thursday: The Commerce Department reports August housing starts.
8. THE NUMBER

That's the target GDP growth rate that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says could solve the nation's debt crunch without relying on tax hikes or spending cuts. With publicly held U.S. debt having crossed 100% of gross domestic product, forecasters say that achieving 3% to 4% growth over a decade could help stabilize the debt ratio. But actually attaining and sustaining that growth is what's difficult.
9. AND FINALLY...
Europe's wealthy are heading north as temperatures climb.

Some Europeans are moving in search of cooler weather and greener pastures. Heat waves, droughts and wildfires are making northern regions of Spain, France and Italy increasingly attractive to buyers. In northern Spain, house prices in some provinces are rising much faster than in Madrid and Barcelona. And cooler summers aren't the only attraction: Some of those making the move point to green fields, beaches, good food and lower house prices.
